body:
_Migrated from issue #995, filed 2026-07-19._

Split out of #941. Credit: @chloeroform, who raised it there.

v4.1.17 narrowed the startup ownership pass to the directories the runtime user actually writes — `metadata_change_logs/` and `metadata_temp/` — instead of re-owning the whole `/app` tree. That removed the cost, but the underlying oddity stands: those directories, and `cps/cache`, live *inside* the application tree, which is read-only code that gets replaced wholesale on every image upgrade.

Consequences today:
- Per-install state sits on a layer that is discarded on upgrade rather than on the `/config` volume where the rest of it lives. #992 was one concrete symptom of the same shape (a per-user marker written to `/app`, which is root-owned and wiped on upgrade).
- The image has to chown parts of its own code tree at boot at all.

Wanted: these directories resolve under `CONFIG_DIR` like other per-install state, with a migration that moves or falls back to the old location so existing volumes are not orphaned, and the startup ownership pass narrows further as a result.

Not scheduled — filing so the idea is tracked rather than buried in a closed thread.
title: Move writable runtime directories (cps/cache, metadata_change_logs, metadata_temp) out of the application tree
